articles.title: Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says
articles.description: Pope Leo had successful surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican said.

articles.title: Saudi man charged with planting 'sophisticated' recording device in OpenAI office
articles.description: Prosecutors say the device, wrapped in toilet paper, was found inserted in a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room.

articles.title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI
articles.description: Sir Ken McCallum says operations to tackle terrorism and state threats are now roughly of an "equal scale".

articles.title: Missiles intercepted near Riyadh after Saudi coalition hits Yemen fuel depot
articles.description: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen struck a fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital, Sanaa.

articles.title: Ex-gang boss sentenced to 40 years for orchestrating Tupac Shakur's murder
articles.description: Davis was found guilty last month over his role in the late rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in 1996.

articles.title: Cornell bans all fraternity parties over gang sex assault allegations
articles.description: The school has faced an uproar over how it handled assault allegations brought by a woman known as Jane Doe.

articles.title: Trump ousts Kimberly Guilfoyle as US ambassador to Greece after corruption allegations
articles.description: Guilfoyle said the allegations of improper conduct were false and that being ambassador was the "honour of a lifetime".

articles.title: Russian strikes hit key power plant in Kyiv, Zelensky says
articles.description: The Ukrainian president says the ballistic missile strikes came with "no early warning from our partners".

articles.title: Horrified witnesses recount fatal rollercoaster incident at Six Flags
articles.description: Police say preliminary information suggests the man who died at the Georgia amusement park fell from a ride.

articles.title: Argentina targets UK in legal claim over Falklands oil exploration
articles.description: The action filed with an international maritime tribunal is the latest development in an escalating row over the Falkland Islands.

articles.title: Watch: Emergency calls from botched Christa Pike execution released
articles.description: A series of calls, obtained by the Associated Press, reveal emergency services were delayed in reaching Pike.

articles.title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34
articles.description: Mitte, who lived with cerebral palsy, starred as Walter White Jr in the Emmy-winning drama series.

articles.title: Bulgaria summons Russian ambassador after ship sinks in Black Sea drone attack
articles.description: Six crew members are rescued but 10 are missing after a merchant ship was sunk overnight, Bulgaria says.

articles.title: BBC FM radio transmissions suspended in Afghanistan
articles.description: BBC programming is still reaching audiences on shortwave, medium wave, via satellite and online.

articles.title: 'I'd talk to the TV': The paid companions bringing warmth to China's lonely
articles.description: As loneliness grows in China, a new industry is emerging to provide companionship and support.

articles.title: Who's to blame for the toxic smog choking South East Asia?
articles.description: Anger is mounting at the companies accused of burning land in Indonesia and the authorities who have failed to stop them.

articles.title: Pakistan has locked down Imran Khan's stronghold - but it could backfire
articles.description: Some fear the government's standoff with the former PM's supporters could bring more instability, not less.

articles.title: Is Zelensky right to say data centre strikes have taken down Russian bots?
articles.description: Experts say there is no evidence that Russian trolls have been affected by Ukraine’s Yandex attacks.

articles.title: The island where locals say data centres are taking their water
articles.description: "Not a single drop has come through our taps for the last three months," a local tells the BBC.

articles.title: Why the lonely in China are hiring 'temporary children'
articles.description: A new industry being dubbed the “loneliness economy” has emerged in China, with people hiring themselves out as companions to help the elderly.

articles.title: Inside Katie Zacharia's very brief White House briefing
articles.description: The BBC's Sarah Smith was in the room and describes Zacharia's performance and the moment she broke news about Kimberly Guilfoyle being asked to resign.

articles.title: 'If we don't scream, they won't listen to us': Student protesters speak to BBC in Paris
articles.description: Student protesters in France have told the BBC's James Waterhouse that they will continue to take action until change has been made. The protests have now entered their fourth week.

articles.title: BBC's Orla Guerin travels with Yemen's southern national security forces through desert battlefield
articles.description: Orla Guerin travelled through Yemen, with forces loyal to its internationally recognised government, to a remote desert battlefield where Houthi rebels were dislodged just days ago.
